title: Docker Registry
subtitle: Publishing, distributing and trusting images
description: A registry is the boundary between build and runtime. Learn authentication, tags and digests, private registries, and the supply-chain controls that make images trustworthy.
outcomes: Authenticate and push to registries safely
Run a private registry with TLS and storage

lessons.title: Registries and authentication
lessons.summary: Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR and self-hosted registries all speak the same distribution API.

sections.title: One API, many providers
sections.body: A registry implements the OCI Distribution API. Docker Hub, GitHub Container Registry, Amazon ECR, Google Artifact Registry and Harbor all accept `docker login`, `push` and `pull`. Image references encode the registry host, so `ghcr.io/acme/api` never goes to Docker Hub.

sections.code:
# Never pass the password as an argument: it lands in shell history.
printf '%s' "$GHCR_TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io -u "$GHCR_USER" --password-stdin

# Inspect the credential configuration (hosts only, not secrets)
docker info --format '{{json .RegistryConfig}}'
cat ~/.docker/config.json

docker logout ghcr.io
sections.note: Docker stores credentials in a credential helper (desktop, pass, secretservice) when configured; otherwise config.json contains base64 auth, not encryption.

sections.title: config.json is not encrypted
sections.body: Base64 is encoding, not encryption. Use a credential helper or short-lived tokens, and never commit ~/.docker/config.json.

exercises.title: Safe login
exercises.prompt: Write a login command using an environment token.

exercises.title: Find the store
exercises.prompt: Check whether a credsStore is configured.

questions.question: Why use --password-stdin?
options: It avoids exposing the password in process lists and history
questions.explain: stdin keeps the secret out of argv and shell history.

questions.question: How does Docker know which registry to push to?
options: The registry host in the image reference
questions.explain: The first reference component selects the registry.

questions.question: What does a credential helper do?
options: Stores credentials in an external secure store
questions.explain: Helpers delegate storage to OS keychains or secret managers.

lessons.title: Tags, digests and publishing
lessons.summary: Tags are convenient and mutable. Digests are precise and immutable. Production needs both, used deliberately.
objectives: Tag an image for a registry

sections.title: The publishing sequence
sections.body: Build with a local name, tag it with the full registry path, push, then read back the digest. The digest is the content identity; deploy by digest when you need an auditable guarantee that the artifact did not change.

sections.code:
docker build -t acme/api:1.4.0 .
docker tag acme/api:1.4.0 ghcr.io/acme/api:1.4.0
docker push ghcr.io/acme/api:1.4.0

docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' ghcr.io/acme/api:1.4.0
# ghcr.io/acme/api@sha256:...

docker pull ghcr.io/acme/api@sha256:abc123...
docker run --rm ghcr.io/acme/api@sha256:abc123... --version
sections.output:
The push refers to repository [ghcr.io/acme/api]
1.4.0: digest: sha256:abc123... size: 1573

sections.title: latest is not a version
sections.body: It is a tag that moves. Deploying latest makes rollbacks ambiguous and caching unpredictable.

exercises.title: Publish
exercises.prompt: Tag and push an image to a registry path.
exercises.expected: docker tag app:1.0 REGISTRY/team/app:1.0 && docker push REGISTRY/team/app:1.0

exercises.title: Pin
exercises.prompt: Write a run command pinned to a digest.

questions.question: Does docker tag push the image?
What does RepoDigests contain?
questions.explain: It maps repository references to content digests.

lessons.title: Run a private registry
lessons.summary: Deploy registry:2 behind TLS, persist its storage, and understand when a managed registry is the better choice.
objectives: Run a registry with persistent storage
Configure TLS or a reverse proxy
Push and pull from the local registry

sections.title: A registry is a stateless-looking HTTP service
sections.body: The reference `registry:2` image implements the distribution API. It stores blobs on the filesystem by default; production deployments put that path on a volume or object storage and terminate TLS in front of it. Without TLS, Docker refuses to authenticate except to localhost.

sections.code:
services:
  registry:
    image: registry:2.8
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5000:5000"
    environment:
      REGISTRY_STORAGE_FILESYSTEM_ROOTDIRECTORY: /var/lib/registry
      REGISTRY_HTTP_ADDR: 0.0.0.0:5000
    volumes:
      - registry-data:/var/lib/registry

volumes:
  registry-data:
sections.note: Localhost HTTP is treated as insecure-but-allowed. For remote access, add TLS or put Caddy/nginx in front.

sections.code:
docker compose up -d
docker tag alpine:3.20 localhost:5000/team/alpine:3.20
docker push localhost:5000/team/alpine:3.20
curl http://localhost:5000/v2/_catalog
curl http://localhost:5000/v2/team/alpine/tags/list

sections.title: The registry has no authentication by default
sections.body: Anyone who can reach the port can push and pull. Put authentication, authorization, TLS and rate limiting in front before exposing it beyond localhost.

exercises.title: Local registry
exercises.prompt: Run registry:2 on 127.0.0.1:5000 with a named volume.
exercises.expected: Use the compose file above and verify /v2/_catalog.

exercises.title: Push to it
exercises.prompt: Tag alpine and push it to localhost:5000/team/alpine:3.20.
exercises.expected: docker tag + docker push, then check the catalog.

questions.question: Why does Docker refuse a remote HTTP registry?
options: It requires TLS for authenticated remote access
questions.explain: Insecure registries must be explicitly allow-listed, which is discouraged.

questions.question: Where should registry blobs live in production?
questions.explain: The writable layer is deleted with the container.

questions.question: Which endpoint lists repositories?
questions.explain: The catalog endpoint is part of the distribution API.
